summary: Security review of the implementation commit e5c789dff plus docs, spanning fa3f11edb..9914d52d4. All audited security properties hold. The dedicated database environment and client factory fail closed on malformed URLs and never echo credentials in errors. The runtime package entrypoint exposes no migration tooling. The grants file revokes all table and sequence privileges from accounting_runtime before granting exactly SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on accounting_submissions and SELECT, INSERT only on accounting_submission_audit_events, with default-privilege revokes and no ALTER ROLE; the durable-owner exclusion list matches marketing. Role provisioning uses NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT with no superuser assumption. The runtime probe plus negative DDL probe use owner-namespaced rows and self-cleanup with no persistent grants. Auth routes fail closed on origin approval, cannot be abused for open redirect, enforce the callback role check after exchange, expire the transaction cookie on every failure path, derive the cookie secure flag from NODE_ENV and resolved protocol, keep the 403 body minimal, and validate the logout origin. cloudbuild.yaml deploys with --tag candidate --no-traffic, scopes the service account, lists exactly the nine contracted secrets, and contains no traffic-shift step. The promotion script requires a non-empty acceptance note containing status: pass with no bypass. Submissions queries remain company-scoped through domain injection with no new unscoped access. No plaintext secrets appear in code, tests, or logs. Verdict pass with three non-blocking observations.
nonblocking_findings: NB-1 (minor): The __Host- prefixed session and transaction cookies now derive the secure flag from NODE_ENV and the resolved origin. In local HTTP development (NODE_ENV=development, http://localhost) the flag resolves to false, so browsers reject the __Host- cookie and local sign-in cannot persist a session. Production and the candidate preview always set secure=true (NODE_ENV=production or https). This is a development ergonomics regression, not a production security exposure. Evidence: apps/accounting/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts:44-45, apps/accounting/app/api/auth/company/start/route.ts:54-56.

NB-2 (info): apps/accounting/app/lib/submissions.ts caches the repository promise in a module-level singleton. A first failed createAccountingRuntimeClient rejects permanently, so the process fails closed with no retry until restart. This is safe because there is no fallback to the main product client, but operations should know a transient connect failure requires a process restart. Evidence: apps/accounting/app/lib/submissions.ts:33-45.

NB-3 (info): connectionTargetFromUrl validates protocol, database name, and login-role pattern but not the presence of a password in the URL. A passwordless URL passes validation and then fails at connect time. This is fail-closed and not exploitable; recorded for completeness. Evidence: packages/db/src/accounting/client.ts:38-77.

evidence: environment.ts fail-closed URL parsing: validateAccountingPostgresUrl rejects surrounding whitespace, non-absolute URLs, non-postgresql protocol, any pathname other than /accounting, and fragments (packages/db/src/accounting/environment.ts:13-60). configurationError (lines 68-78) formats Zod issues from static messages plus field names only, never the URL value, so no secret can leak into error text.

Runtime client factory exposes no migration tooling: packages/db/src/accounting/runtime.ts re-exports only createAccountingRuntimeClient. createAccountingDirectClient and migrateAccounting live in client.ts and migration.ts, which the package.json exports map does not expose; only ./accounting/runtime and ./accounting/schema are public subpaths.

Runtime URL target enforced at the client boundary: connectionTargetFromUrl requires postgresql protocol, no fragment, database name exactly accounting, and a login role matching ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$ (packages/db/src/accounting/client.ts:38-77). submissions.ts passes process.env.ACCOUNTING_DATABASE_URL ?? "", which fails closed when unset.

Grants revoke-first ordering and exact privilege set: accounting-runtime-grants.sql revokes all table privileges (lines 34/56) and sequence privileges (lines 83/123) from accounting_runtime before granting SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on accounting_submissions (line 135) and SELECT, INSERT only on accounting_submission_audit_events (line 137). No UPDATE or DELETE grant on the audit table, so append-only is enforced by grants.

Grants have no ALTER ROLE and revoke future defaults: no ALTER ROLE statement exists; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE CURRENT_USER revokes table and sequence privileges from PUBLIC and accounting_runtime (lines 141-148). REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC and FROM accounting_runtime (lines 13-14) makes the runtime role unable to create tables.

Durable-owner exclusion parity: the exclusion lists (owners durable_job_audit_owner and durable_job_queue_runtime; tables durable_job_audit_events and review_job_adoption_audit_events) match apps/marketing/scripts/marketing-runtime-grants.sql exactly.

Role provisioning posture: accounting-runtime-role-provision.sql creates both roles with LOGIN PASSWORD %L NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT (lines 24, 30), uses quote_literal via %L to prevent SQL injection in passwords, requires both password variables with \if fail-closed checks, and contains no SUPERUSER grant.

Runtime probe and negative DDL probe: accounting-runtime-probe.sql exercises application insert/update/select, proves an audit INSERT is allowed, asserts audit UPDATE and DELETE raise insufficient_privilege, and asserts CREATE TABLE raises insufficient_privilege (negative DDL). Rows are namespaced by probe_owner_id and cleaned up by accounting-runtime-probe-cleanup.sql via a trap in cloudbuild.yaml; the probe grants nothing.

Origin approval fail-closed: public-url.ts getPublicOrigin accepts forwarded proto/host only when the resulting origin is the canonical origin, the callback origin, an ACCOUNTING_PREVIEW_ORIGINS entry, or localhost in development, and throws PUBLIC_ORIGIN_INVALID otherwise. Callers fall back to the callback origin (callback, start), the canonical origin (proxy), or a 403 (logout).

Preview handoff cannot be abused for open redirect: the start route only redirects to new URL(requestUrl.pathname, callbackOrigin), a fixed approved origin, with a returnTo already validated by parseCompanyOidcReturnTo; the target is never attacker-controlled.

returnTo validation: parseCompanyOidcReturnTo delegates to isSafeRelativeReturnPath, which rejects anything not matching ^/(?!//)[^\\]*$ plus control characters, so https://evil.example.com and protocol-relative //host are rejected and the start route restarts with returnTo=/ (packages/auth/src/company-identity/client.ts:74-81,97-99).

Callback role check and cookie cleanup: callback checks resolveAccountingRole(session.identity.roles) after exchange and before setting the session cookie, revokes the token on denial, and redirects to /login?error=forbidden (apps/accounting/app/api/auth/callback/route.ts:65-82). Every failure path (missing transaction/code/state, no-role, exchange throw) calls expireTransactionCookie.

Session 403 shape reveals nothing extra: the no-role 403 body is {"session": null, "denied": true}, matching Sales parity; 401 keeps {"session": null} and 200 keeps {"session": {"user": ...}} (apps/accounting/app/api/auth/session/route.ts:18-24).
Logout origin validated: logout returns 403 when getPublicOrigin throws or when the Origin header does not equal the approved origin (apps/accounting/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts:29-43).

cloudbuild.yaml candidate and secrets: deploy step uses --tag=candidate --no-traffic (line 64), --service-account=accounting-cloud-run@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com (line 56), and contains no traffic-shift step. availableSecrets lists exactly the nine contracted secrets (DIRECT_DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL, COMPANY_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, six STORAGE_*), with no extras.

Promotion gate: promote-accounting-candidate.sh requires CANDIDATE_REVISION and a non-empty ACCEPTANCE_NOTE whose contents include the exact line status: pass (grep -Eq '^status: pass$'), with no bypass path, then shifts 100 percent traffic.

Multi-tenancy scoping preserved: the accounting domain derives scope from actor.companyId via actorScope (packages/backend/src/modules/accounting/submissions.ts:149-151) and never accepts caller-supplied scope; the diff only swaps the injected client. The tenant registry keeps both tables EXEMPT via the new schema entrypoint (packages/domain/src/tenant-registry.ts:196-197).

Secrets scan clean: a scan of the changed and new files found no private-key, AKIA, or hardcoded credential material. The only postgresql:// URL with embedded credentials is the local development placeholder postgres:postgres@localhost in pre-existing .env files, which are outside the diff. The drizzle config fallback uses configuration-required@generation-only.invalid, a non-secret placeholder.

Accounting journal isolation: packages/db/accounting/drizzle/0000_past_reavers.sql creates only accounting_submissions and accounting_submission_audit_events and their indexes/checks; the main-journal tip snapshot 0056_snapshot.json retains zero accounting references after pruning.
